items: Commits "disappeared" after switching branches. Root cause: they were made in detached HEAD and were reachable only through HEAD; git reflog shows them, and git branch <name> <id> brings them back.
Treating the detached-HEAD message as an error to make go away. Root cause: it is a normal state that Git itself uses for bisect and rebase; the message is advice.
A script that calls git branch --show-current fails in CI. Root cause: CI jobs, deploy checkouts and submodules are in detached HEAD, and the command prints nothing there.
git push with no refspec from a deploy checkout does nothing useful. Root cause: no branch is current; use git rev-parse HEAD for the commit, and name the branch explicitly when pushing.
Assuming an interrupted rebase broke the branch. Root cause: a rebase runs on a detached HEAD and moves the branch only at the end.

beats.text: Your CTO has a calm question: "A contractor says two days of work vanished after she 'checked out a tag to test something'. Is it gone?"
beats.tele: Your CTO has a calm question: "A contractor says two days of work vanished after she 'checked out a tag to test something'. Is it gone?"

beats.text: She checked out a tag, a fixed name for one commit. She kept working, and committed, for two days. Then she switched back to main, and her commits aren't in any log she knows how to read. Gone, or not? Say it out loud.
beats.tele: She checked out a tag, a fixed name for one commit. She kept working, and committed, for two days. Then she switched back to `main`, and her commits aren't in any log she knows how to read. Gone, or not? Say it out loud.

beats.text: No, it's not gone. The commits exist, and are recoverable from the reflog, Git's local diary of where HEAD has been. And Git told her so at the moment she left: it printed a warning, named the commits, and printed the command that would have kept them. This video is about the state she was in, why it's normal, and why one command is enough to keep work made there. Remember that warning. You'll read it yourself in the demo.

beats.text: In one sentence. HEAD is detached when it holds a commit ID instead of a branch name. Git works normally, and new commits advance HEAD itself rather than any branch. Here HEAD sits on the tagged commit, not on main.
beats.tele: In one sentence. HEAD is detached when it holds a commit ID instead of a branch name. Git works normally, and new commits advance HEAD itself rather than any branch. Here HEAD sits on the tagged commit, not on `main`.

beats.text: Precisely. The manual says that in detached HEAD state "HEAD refers to a specific commit, as opposed to referring to a named branch", and that a commit made there "is referenced only by HEAD". Git detaches HEAD whenever you ask for a commit that no branch names, and several commands do it for you.
beats.tele: Precisely. The manual says that in detached HEAD state "HEAD refers to a specific commit, as opposed to referring to a named branch", and that a commit made there "is referenced only by HEAD". Git detaches HEAD whenever you ask for a commit that no branch names, and several commands do it for you.

beats.text: Recall the state table from video 19. git commit in detached HEAD sets HEAD to the new commit ID. There is no current branch, no branch moves, and one line is written in logs/HEAD only.
beats.tele: Recall the state table from video 19. `git commit` in detached HEAD sets HEAD to the new commit ID. There is no current branch, no branch moves, and one line is written in `logs/HEAD` only.

beats.text: Quick quiz. You made these two commits while detached, and now you switch to main. What happens to them? A, Git deletes them. B, they move onto main. C, they stay, with no name. Your answer?
beats.tele: Quick quiz. You made these two commits while detached, and now you switch to `main`. What happens to them? A, Git deletes them. B, they move onto `main`. C, they stay, with no name. Your answer?

beats.text: What happens when you leave. The answer is C. Commits made while detached are reachable only through HEAD. Once HEAD moves to a branch, no ref reaches them. They still exist as objects, and the reflog of HEAD still refers to them.
beats.tele: What happens when you leave. The answer is C. Commits made while detached are reachable only through HEAD. Once HEAD moves to a branch, no ref reaches them. They still exist as objects, and the reflog of HEAD still refers to them.

beats.text: Three ways to ask "which branch am I on". Each answers differently when the answer is "none". git symbolic-ref HEAD fails with status 128. git branch --show-current prints nothing. git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD prints the literal word HEAD. Scripts must handle all three.
beats.tele: Three ways to ask "which branch am I on". Each answers differently when the answer is "none". `git symbolic-ref HEAD` fails with status 128. `git branch --show-current` prints nothing. `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` prints the literal word `HEAD`. Scripts must handle all three.

beats.text: Where git status gets its words. It reads the HEAD reflog backwards for the latest checkout: moving from ... to X entry. X is printed after "at" if HEAD still equals that entry's commit, and after "from" otherwise. With no such entry, as in a fresh clone, it prints Not currently on any branch. The textbook cites the Git 2.55.0 source for this.
beats.tele: Where `git status` gets its words. It reads the HEAD reflog backwards for the latest `checkout: moving from ... to X` entry. X is printed after "at" if HEAD still equals that entry's commit, and after "from" otherwise. With no such entry, as in a fresh clone, it prints `Not currently on any branch.` The textbook cites the Git 2.55.0 source for this.

beats.text: Every way it happens.
beats.tele: Every way it happens.

beats.text: Checking out a tag. Checking out a commit by ID, or by a relative name such as HEAD~1. Checking out a remote-tracking branch such as origin/main. git bisect, a binary search over commits: every step checks out a commit to test. git rebase, while it runs or is stopped. The rebase replays commits on a detached HEAD, and moves the branch only at the end. That's why an interrupted rebase looks like a detached HEAD: it is one.
beats.tele: Checking out a tag. Checking out a commit by ID, or by a relative name such as `HEAD~1`. Checking out a remote-tracking branch such as `origin/main`. `git bisect`, a binary search over commits: every step checks out a commit to test. `git rebase`, while it runs or is stopped. The rebase replays commits on a detached HEAD, and moves the branch only at the end. That's why an interrupted rebase looks like a detached HEAD: it is one.

beats.text: git clone --branch <tag>: a clone of one release, the shape of many deploy scripts. git worktree add with a tag or a commit. git submodule update: the default mode puts each submodule on a detached HEAD, and that one is not run here. And a CI checkout, the copy an automated build job works in.

beats.text: Keeping the work. Three commands create a ref for the commit HEAD is on, as the manual lists them. git switch -c <name> attaches HEAD to a new branch there. git branch <name> creates the branch and leaves HEAD detached. git tag <name> creates a tag. All three are 🟢 SAFE: each adds a ref. After you've moved away, find the ID in git reflog first.
beats.tele: Keeping the work. Three commands create a ref for the commit HEAD is on, as the manual lists them. `git switch -c <name>` attaches HEAD to a new branch there. `git branch <name>` creates the branch and leaves HEAD detached. `git tag <name>` creates a tag. All three are 🟢 SAFE: each adds a ref. After you've moved away, find the ID in `git reflog` first.

beats.text: When to use it, and when not. Use it on purpose to look at an old state, to test a release, to try an experiment you may throw away. Don't leave it with commits you want and no name for them. The rule for people is one sentence: before you leave a detached HEAD with commits on it, give them a branch.

beats.text: Five mistakes to watch for.
beats.tele: Five mistakes to watch for.

beats.text: Commits "disappeared" after switching branches. Root cause: they were made in detached HEAD and were reachable only through HEAD; git reflog shows them, and git branch <name> <id> brings them back.
beats.tele: Commits "disappeared" after switching branches. Root cause: they were made in detached HEAD and were reachable only through HEAD; `git reflog` shows them, and `git branch <name> <id>` brings them back.

beats.text: Treating the detached-HEAD message as an error to make go away. Root cause: it is a normal state that Git itself uses for bisect and rebase; the message is advice.
beats.tele: Treating the detached-HEAD message as an error to make go away. Root cause: it is a normal state that Git itself uses for bisect and rebase; the message is advice.

beats.text: A script that calls git branch --show-current fails in CI. Root cause: CI jobs, deploy checkouts and submodules are in detached HEAD, and the command prints nothing there.
beats.tele: A script that calls `git branch --show-current` fails in CI. Root cause: CI jobs, deploy checkouts and submodules are in detached HEAD, and the command prints nothing there.

beats.text: git push with no refspec from a deploy checkout does nothing useful. Root cause: no branch is current; use git rev-parse HEAD for the commit, and name the branch explicitly when pushing.
beats.tele: `git push` with no refspec from a deploy checkout does nothing useful. Root cause: no branch is current; use `git rev-parse HEAD` for the commit, and name the branch explicitly when pushing.

beats.text: Assuming an interrupted rebase broke the branch. Root cause: a rebase runs on a detached HEAD and moves the branch only at the end.
beats.tele: Assuming an interrupted rebase broke the branch. Root cause: a rebase runs on a detached HEAD and moves the branch only at the end.

beats.text: Now, out of the lab. The textbook states the production rule in one paragraph. Detached HEAD is the normal state of a CI job, a deploy checkout and a submodule, so a script that assumes a current branch fails in exactly those places.
beats.tele: Now, out of the lab. The textbook states the production rule in one paragraph. Detached HEAD is the normal state of a CI job, a deploy checkout and a submodule, so a script that assumes a current branch fails in exactly those places.

beats.text: An ML team's release job clones the repository at a tag, generates a model card, commits it, and pushes. The commit succeeds, onto nothing. The push has no refspec, meaning it names no branch, so it has no branch to push. The repaired job uses git rev-parse HEAD to record the commit it built from, creates a branch with git switch -c before committing, and names that branch in the push.
beats.tele: An ML team's release job clones the repository at a tag, generates a model card, commits it, and pushes. The commit succeeds, onto nothing. The push has no refspec, meaning it names no branch, so it has no branch to push. The repaired job uses `git rev-parse HEAD` to record the commit it built from, creates a branch with `git switch -c` before committing, and names that branch in the push.

beats.tele: Your turn. Do Lab 4.2, "Detached HEAD rescue", in `lab-manual/m04-refs-branches-head.md`.

beats.text: Before you leave the detached HEAD in the lab, write down what you expect in three places afterwards: git log --all, git reflog, and git fsck. Then switch away and compare.
beats.tele: Before you leave the detached HEAD in the lab, write down what you expect in three places afterwards: `git log --all`, `git reflog`, and `git fsck`. Then switch away and compare.

beats.text: Q98: "A colleague's two days of commits are "gone" after she checked out a tag and later switched back to main. Walk through the recovery and explain why it works."
beats.tele: Q98: "A colleague's two days of commits are "gone" after she checked out a tag and later switched back to `main`. Walk through the recovery and explain why it works."

beats.text: Answer out loud. A strong answer starts with the state of HEAD after the checkout, and says which ref her commits moved. It names where the IDs can still be found, and the one command that makes them reachable. It explains why the objects were never in danger at that point, and says what the time limit is. Mention what Git printed when she switched away.
beats.tele: Answer out loud. A strong answer starts with the state of HEAD after the checkout, and says which ref her commits moved. It names where the IDs can still be found, and the one command that makes them reachable. It explains why the objects were never in danger at that point, and says what the time limit is. Mention what Git printed when she switched away.

beats.text: Let's land this. You should now be able to say: detached HEAD means .git/HEAD holds a commit ID instead of a branch name. It's a normal state, entered by checking out a tag, a commit or a remote-tracking branch, and by bisect, rebase, a clone at a tag, a worktree from a tag, submodules and CI checkouts.
beats.tele: Let's land this. You should now be able to say: detached HEAD means `.git/HEAD` holds a commit ID instead of a branch name. It's a normal state, entered by checking out a tag, a commit or a remote-tracking branch, and by bisect, rebase, a clone at a tag, a worktree from a tag, submodules and CI checkouts.

beats.text: Commits made there advance HEAD only. When I switch away, Git names the commits and prints the command that keeps them. Afterwards the HEAD reflog still has their IDs. Keeping the work is one command: create a branch.
beats.tele: Commits made there advance HEAD only. When I switch away, Git names the commits and prints the command that keeps them. Afterwards the HEAD reflog still has their IDs. Keeping the work is one command: create a branch.
